title.en: SAT R&W: Cross-Text Connections: the point of contact
title.uz: SAT R&W: Cross-Text Connections — ikki matn tutashgan nuqta
title.ru: SAT R&W: Cross-Text Connections — точка соприкосновения двух текстов

body.en:
Lesson 1 named the relation between two texts: they agree, disagree or agree in part. Harder questions need one more step: find the point of contact, the exact part of Text 1 that Text 2 answers.
1. Split Text 1 into its parts:
• the finding: what happened or what someone noticed
• the cause: why someone thinks it happened
• the method: how someone found out
• the plan: what someone wants to do
2. Ask which part Text 2 answers. Text 2 often accepts the finding and argues about the cause, or accepts the goal of a plan and argues about its price.
3. Name how Text 2 answers it:
• another cause: something else may explain the result
• a limit: true only in some cases, or only for a short time
• a new case: the same idea works somewhere else too
• a cost: a problem Text 1 left out
The right option names the right part and the right how. The question often names the part for you: "How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation in Text 1?"
body.uz:
1-darsda ikki matn orasidagi bogʻliqlikni nomladik: rozi, rozi emas yoki qisman rozi. Qiyinroq savollar yana bir qadamni talab qiladi: tutashgan nuqtani, yaʼni Text 2 javob berayotgan Text 1 ning aynan qaysi qismini toping.
1. Text 1 ni qismlarga ajrating:
• topilma: nima boʻldi yoki kimdir nimani payqadi
• sabab: kimdir bu nega boʻldi deb oʻylaydi
• usul: kimdir buni qanday aniqladi
• reja: kimdir nima qilmoqchi
2. Text 2 qaysi qismga javob berayotganini aniqlang. Koʻpincha Text 2 topilmani qabul qilib, sabab haqida bahslashadi yoki rejaning maqsadini qabul qilib, uning narxi haqida bahslashadi.
3. Text 2 qanday javob berishini nomlang:
• boshqa sabab: natijani boshqa narsa tushuntirishi mumkin
• cheklov: faqat baʼzi hollarda yoki faqat qisqa vaqt toʻgʻri
• yangi holat: xuddi shu gʻoya boshqa joyda ham ishlaydi
• xarajat: Text 1 aytmay qoldirgan muammo
Toʻgʻri variant toʻgʻri qismni ham, toʻgʻri javob turini ham nomlaydi. Koʻpincha savolning oʻzi qismni aytadi: «How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation in Text 1?»
body.ru:
В уроке 1 мы называли связь двух текстов: согласны, не согласны или согласны частично. Трудные вопросы требуют ещё одного шага: найдите точку соприкосновения — ту часть Text 1, на которую отвечает Text 2.
1. Разделите Text 1 на части:
• наблюдение: что произошло или что кто-то заметил
• причина: почему, по чьему-то мнению, это произошло
• метод: как кто-то это выяснил
• план: что кто-то хочет сделать
2. Спросите, на какую часть отвечает Text 2. Часто Text 2 принимает наблюдение и спорит о причине или принимает цель плана и спорит о его цене.
3. Назовите, как Text 2 отвечает:
• другая причина: результат может объяснять что-то другое
• ограничение: верно лишь в некоторых случаях или лишь недолго
• новый случай: та же мысль работает и в другом месте
• цена: проблема, которую Text 1 упустил
Верный вариант называет и нужную часть, и нужный ответ. Часто вопрос сам называет часть: «How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the explanation in Text 1?»

body.en:
Worked example.
Text 1: our class grew beans on the windowsill, and they grew fast; the teacher says the new plant food did it.
Text 2: the beans did grow fast, but the class also began watering them every day.
Part of Text 1 that Text 2 answers: not the finding (both say the beans grew fast) but the cause.
How: another cause. Text 2 would say the daily watering may explain the growth.
Now you:
Text 1
Last autumn, the school library moved its soft chairs from a dark corner to the big windows. By December, students were borrowing a third more books than before. The librarian, Ms. Karimova, believes that the better light is what made students want to read.

Text 2
Borrowing at the library did rise last autumn. In the same months, however, the English teachers started a reading contest, and students earned points for every book they took home. A rise that large may owe more to the contest than to the chairs.
1. The finding: borrowing rose. Text 2 accepts it ("Borrowing at the library did rise").
2. The part Text 2 answers: the explanation of the librarian, the light.
3. How does Text 2 answer it?
body.uz:
Namuna.
Text 1: sinfimiz deraza tokchasida loviya oʻstirdi, ular tez oʻsdi; oʻqituvchining aytishicha, bunga yangi oʻgʻit sabab boʻlgan.
Text 2: loviya rostdan tez oʻsdi, lekin sinf ularni har kuni sugʻorishni ham boshlagan edi.
Text 2 javob bergan qism: topilma emas (ikkalasi ham loviya tez oʻsdi deydi), balki sabab.
Qanday: boshqa sabab. Text 2 oʻsishni har kungi sugʻorish tushuntirishi mumkin, der edi.
Endi siz:
Text 1
Last autumn, the school library moved its soft chairs from a dark corner to the big windows. By December, students were borrowing a third more books than before. The librarian, Ms. Karimova, believes that the better light is what made students want to read.

Text 2
Borrowing at the library did rise last autumn. In the same months, however, the English teachers started a reading contest, and students earned points for every book they took home. A rise that large may owe more to the contest than to the chairs.
1. Topilma: kitob olish koʻpaydi. Text 2 buni qabul qiladi («Borrowing at the library did rise»).
2. Text 2 javob bergan qism: kutubxonachining tushuntirishi, yaʼni yorugʻlik.
3. Text 2 unga qanday javob beradi?
body.ru:
Разбор.
Text 1: наш класс вырастил фасоль на подоконнике, она росла быстро; учитель говорит, что помогла новая подкормка.
Text 2: фасоль правда росла быстро, но класс тогда же начал поливать её каждый день.
Часть Text 1, на которую отвечает Text 2: не наблюдение (оба говорят, что фасоль росла быстро), а причина.
Как: другая причина. Text 2 сказал бы, что рост может объяснять ежедневный полив.
Теперь попробуйте сами:
Text 1
Last autumn, the school library moved its soft chairs from a dark corner to the big windows. By December, students were borrowing a third more books than before. The librarian, Ms. Karimova, believes that the better light is what made students want to read.

Text 2
Borrowing at the library did rise last autumn. In the same months, however, the English teachers started a reading contest, and students earned points for every book they took home. A rise that large may owe more to the contest than to the chairs.
1. Наблюдение: книг стали брать больше. Text 2 это принимает («Borrowing at the library did rise»).
2. Часть, на которую отвечает Text 2: объяснение библиотекаря — свет.
3. Как Text 2 на неё отвечает?

body.en:
Watch out: an option can name the right part with the wrong how, or the right how with the wrong part.
1. The wrong part. If Text 2 says "yes, sales rose, but the reason is different", it accepts the finding. An option saying that Text 2 doubts the rise is wrong.
2. A cost is not a failure. If Text 2 grants that a plan would work and names its price, an option saying that "the plan would not work" goes too far.
3. A limit is not a rejection. "Not for very young children" or "not after the summer" is not "never".
Test every option with two questions: which part of Text 1 does it name, and how does Text 2 answer that part?
body.uz:
Ehtiyot boʻling: variant toʻgʻri qismni notoʻgʻri javob turi bilan yoki toʻgʻri javob turini notoʻgʻri qism bilan aytishi mumkin.
1. Notoʻgʻri qism. Agar Text 2 «yes, sales rose, but the reason is different» desa, u topilmani qabul qiladi. Text 2 oʻsishga shubha qiladi degan variant xato.
2. Xarajat — muvaffaqiyatsizlik emas. Text 2 reja ishlashini tan olib, uning narxini aytsa, «the plan would not work» degan variant haddan oshadi.
3. Cheklov — rad etish emas. «Not for very young children» yoki «not after the summer» — bu «never» emas.
Har bir variantni ikki savol bilan tekshiring: u Text 1 ning qaysi qismini aytadi va Text 2 oʻsha qismga qanday javob beradi?
body.ru:
Осторожно: вариант может назвать нужную часть с неверным ответом или верный ответ к чужой части.
1. Не та часть. Если Text 2 говорит «yes, sales rose, but the reason is different», он принимает наблюдение. Вариант, где Text 2 сомневается в росте, неверен.
2. Цена — не провал. Если Text 2 признаёт, что план сработает, и называет его цену, вариант «the plan would not work» заходит слишком далеко.
3. Ограничение — не отрицание. «Not for very young children» или «not after the summer» — это не «never».
Проверяйте каждый вариант двумя вопросами: какую часть Text 1 он называет и как Text 2 отвечает на эту часть?

title.en: SAT R&W: Cross-Text Connections: agreement and the other direction
title.uz: SAT R&W: Cross-Text Connections — umumiy fikr va teskari yoʻnalish
title.ru: SAT R&W: Cross-Text Connections — в чём согласны оба автора и вопрос в обратную сторону

body.en:
Two more question types finish this unit.
1. "Both authors would most likely agree with which statement?" Two texts that argue often share a fact. Write three short lines:
• Facts: what does each text accept as true?
• Reason: why does each author think it happens?
• Action: what does each author want done?
The authors often agree on the facts and split on the reason or the action. The right option sits on a line where both texts say the same thing.
2. "How would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to …?" The direction is reversed. Text 1 was not written as an answer to Text 2, so take the view of Text 1 and apply it to the claim in Text 2: would its author accept it, reject it or accept it in part?
The texts here are often formal and dense. First say each in one line: "Text 1: X, because Y."
body.uz:
Bu boʻlimni yana ikki savol turi yakunlaydi.
1. «Both authors would most likely agree with which statement?» (ikkala muallif qaysi fikrga rozi boʻlardi?) Bahslashayotgan ikki matn koʻpincha bitta faktda kelishadi. Uchta qisqa qator yozing:
• Faktlar: har bir matn nimani rost deb qabul qiladi?
• Sabab: har bir muallif bu nega boʻladi deb oʻylaydi?
• Harakat: har bir muallif nima qilinishini xohlaydi?
Mualliflar koʻpincha faktlarda kelishadi, sabab yoki harakatda esa ajralishadi. Toʻgʻri variant ikkala matn bir xil gapirgan qatorda turadi.
2. «How would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to …?» Yoʻnalish teskari. Text 1 Text 2 ga javob sifatida yozilmagan, shuning uchun Text 1 qarashini olib, Text 2 dagi daʼvoga qoʻllang: uning muallifi buni qabul qiladimi, rad etadimi yoki qisman qabul qiladimi?
Bu yerdagi matnlar koʻpincha rasmiy va zich. Avval har birini bir qatorda ayting: «Text 1: X, chunki Y».
body.ru:
Этот раздел завершают ещё два типа вопросов.
1. «Both authors would most likely agree with which statement?» (с каким утверждением согласились бы оба автора?) Спорящие тексты часто сходятся в каком-то факте. Запишите три короткие строки:
• Факты: что каждый текст принимает за правду?
• Причина: почему, по мнению каждого автора, так происходит?
• Действие: чего хочет каждый автор?
Авторы часто согласны в фактах и расходятся в причине или в действии. Верный вариант стоит на той строке, где оба текста говорят одно и то же.
2. «How would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to …?» Направление обратное. Text 1 написан не как ответ на Text 2, поэтому встаньте на точку зрения Text 1 и примените её к утверждению Text 2: примет ли его автор, отвергнет или примет частично?
Тексты здесь часто официальные и плотные. Сначала перескажите каждый одной строкой: «Text 1: X, потому что Y».

body.en:
Worked example.
Text 1: the new traffic light outside our school has made mornings safer, because drivers now stop.
Text 2: mornings are safer, but because a teacher now stands at the crossing.
Facts: both say mornings are safer. Reason: the light or the teacher. Action: none.
So both authors would agree: mornings at the crossing are safer now.
Now you:
Text 1
Shoppers in our district now carry home far fewer plastic bags than they did five years ago. The reason, in my view, is the small fee that shops began charging for each bag: people dislike paying for something that used to be free, however little it costs.

Text 2
There is no doubt that fewer plastic bags leave the shops in our district today. The fee, though, is too small to change how people shop. What changed them was the school campaign in which children sewed and decorated cloth bags and took them home; parents simply use the bags their children made.
Reason: Text 1, the fee. Text 2, the cloth bags the children made. They split here.
Action: neither text asks for anything.
Facts: what does each text say about the number of plastic bags, and which statement would both authors accept?
body.uz:
Namuna.
Text 1: maktabimiz oldidagi yangi svetofor ertalabki qatnovni xavfsizroq qildi, chunki haydovchilar endi toʻxtaydi.
Text 2: ertalablari xavfsizroq, lekin buning sababi — endi oʻtish joyida oʻqituvchi turadi.
Faktlar: ikkalasi ham ertalablari xavfsizroq deydi. Sabab: svetofor yoki oʻqituvchi. Harakat: yoʻq.
Demak, ikkala muallif rozi boʻladi: oʻtish joyida ertalablari endi xavfsizroq.
Endi siz:
Text 1
Shoppers in our district now carry home far fewer plastic bags than they did five years ago. The reason, in my view, is the small fee that shops began charging for each bag: people dislike paying for something that used to be free, however little it costs.

Text 2
There is no doubt that fewer plastic bags leave the shops in our district today. The fee, though, is too small to change how people shop. What changed them was the school campaign in which children sewed and decorated cloth bags and took them home; parents simply use the bags their children made.
Sabab: Text 1 — toʻlov. Text 2 — bolalar tikkan mato sumkalar. Shu yerda ajralishadi.
Harakat: hech bir matn hech narsa talab qilmaydi.
Faktlar: har bir matn plastik paketlar soni haqida nima deydi va ikkala muallif qaysi fikrni qabul qiladi?
body.ru:
Разбор.
Text 1: новый светофор у нашей школы сделал утро безопаснее, потому что водители теперь останавливаются.
Text 2: утром безопаснее, но потому, что у перехода теперь стоит учитель.
Факты: оба говорят, что утром безопаснее. Причина: светофор или учитель. Действие: нет.
Значит, оба автора согласились бы: утром у перехода теперь безопаснее.
Теперь попробуйте сами:
Text 1
Shoppers in our district now carry home far fewer plastic bags than they did five years ago. The reason, in my view, is the small fee that shops began charging for each bag: people dislike paying for something that used to be free, however little it costs.

Text 2
There is no doubt that fewer plastic bags leave the shops in our district today. The fee, though, is too small to change how people shop. What changed them was the school campaign in which children sewed and decorated cloth bags and took them home; parents simply use the bags their children made.
Причина: Text 1 — плата. Text 2 — тканевые сумки, которые сшили дети. Здесь они расходятся.
Действие: ни один текст ничего не требует.
Факты: что каждый текст говорит о числе пакетов и с каким утверждением согласились бы оба автора?

body.en:
Watch out for four traps.
1. One author only. In a "both agree" question, the reason or the action that only one author gives is a trap. Check the facts line first.
2. Mentioned is not agreed. Text 2 may repeat a view only to reject it. A view that appears in both texts is not always a view both hold.
3. The wrong voice. When the question asks how the author of Text 1 would respond, one option usually gives the view of Text 2. Answer as the author of Text 1.
4. Too strong. Two authors who share a fact rarely share an "always" or a "never".
body.uz:
Toʻrtta tuzoqdan ehtiyot boʻling.
1. Faqat bitta muallif. «Both agree» savolida faqat bitta muallif aytgan sabab yoki harakat — tuzoq. Avval faktlar qatorini tekshiring.
2. Tilga olingan — rozi boʻlingan degani emas. Text 2 fikrni faqat rad etish uchun takrorlashi mumkin. Ikkala matnda uchragan fikr har doim ham ikkalasining fikri emas.
3. Notoʻgʻri ovoz. Savol Text 1 muallifi qanday javob berishini soʻrasa, bitta variant odatda Text 2 fikrini beradi. Text 1 muallifi sifatida javob bering.
4. Haddan kuchli. Bitta faktda kelishgan ikki muallif kamdan-kam hollarda «always» yoki «never» da ham kelishadi.
body.ru:
Осторожно, четыре ловушки.
1. Только один автор. В вопросе «both agree» причина или действие, которые называет лишь один автор, — ловушка. Сначала проверьте строку фактов.
2. Упомянуто — не значит принято. Text 2 может повторить мнение, только чтобы его отвергнуть. Мнение, которое есть в обоих текстах, не всегда разделяют оба.
3. Чужой голос. Если вопрос о том, как ответил бы автор Text 1, один вариант обычно передаёт взгляд Text 2. Отвечайте как автор Text 1.
4. Слишком сильно. Два автора, согласные в факте, редко согласны в «always» или «never».

title.en: SAT R&W: Inferences: what a comparison shows
title.ru: SAT R&W: Inferences — вывод из сравнения

body.en:
Many inference texts describe a comparison: two groups, two pots or two weeks that differ in one thing. The blank asks what the comparison shows.
1. List what was the same for both: the place, the time, the people, the amounts.
2. Find the one thing that was different.
3. Compare the results.
4. Say what the difference in results shows about that one thing, and only about it.
If the results differ, the one difference most likely caused it. If the results are the same, that thing made little or no difference, at least in this test.
Example: two classes read the same story in the same lesson; one heard it read aloud, the other read it silently. The first class answered more questions about it, so hearing the story most likely helped these students.
body.uz:
Koʻp Inferences matnlari taqqoslashni tasvirlaydi: bitta narsada farq qiladigan ikki guruh, ikki tuvak yoki ikki hafta. Boʻsh joy taqqoslash nimani koʻrsatishini soʻraydi.
1. Ikkalasida nima bir xil boʻlganini yozing: joy, vaqt, odamlar, miqdorlar.
2. Farq qilgan yagona narsani toping.
3. Natijalarni solishtiring.
4. Natijalardagi farq aynan shu narsa haqida nimani koʻrsatishini ayting, faqat shu haqda.
Natijalar farq qilsa, bu farqqa ehtimol oʻsha yagona farq sabab boʻlgan. Natijalar bir xil boʻlsa, oʻsha narsa hech boʻlmaganda shu sinovda deyarli taʼsir qilmagan.
Misol: ikki sinf bir darsda bitta hikoyani oʻqidi; biriga u ovoz chiqarib oʻqib berildi, ikkinchisi uni ichida oʻqidi. Birinchi sinf u haqida koʻproq savolga javob berdi, demak hikoyani tinglash bu oʻquvchilarga ehtimol yordam bergan.
body.ru:
Многие тексты Inferences описывают сравнение: две группы, два горшка или две недели, которые различаются чем-то одним. В пропуске нужно сказать, что показывает сравнение.
1. Перечислите, что было одинаково: место, время, люди, количества.
2. Найдите единственное различие.
3. Сравните результаты.
4. Скажите, что разница в результатах показывает об этом одном различии — и только о нём.
Если результаты разные, их, вероятно, вызвало это различие. Если результаты одинаковы, это различие почти ни на что не повлияло — по крайней мере в этой проверке.
Пример: два класса на одном уроке читали один рассказ; одному его читали вслух, другой читал про себя. Первый класс ответил на большее число вопросов, значит, слушание, вероятно, помогло этим ученикам.

body.en:
Worked example: "Aziza grew mint in two identical pots on the same windowsill, with the same soil and water. She watered one pot every day and the other every third day. The pot watered every day wilted and turned yellow."
Same: the pots, the sill, the soil, the water.
Different: how often she watered.
Result: the daily pot did worse. So, for this mint, watering every day was most likely too often.
Now you: "Two neighbors, Farrux and Jasur, built identical wooden birdhouses from the same plan and hung them on the same day at the same height. Farrux hung his on a tree in a quiet corner of his garden; Jasur hung his on a tree of the same kind beside his busy front gate. By June, birds were nesting in the birdhouse in the garden, while the one by the gate stayed empty. The birds most likely chose the birdhouse ______"
Same: the plan, the day, the height, the kind of tree.
Different: a quiet corner of a garden or a busy front gate.
Result: birds nest only in the garden birdhouse.
What does the one difference show?
body.uz:
Namuna: «Aziza grew mint in two identical pots on the same windowsill, with the same soil and water. She watered one pot every day and the other every third day. The pot watered every day wilted and turned yellow.»
Bir xil: tuvaklar, tokcha, tuproq, suv.
Farq: qanchalik tez-tez sugʻorgani.
Natija: har kuni sugʻorilgan tuvak yomonroq. Demak, bu yalpiz uchun har kuni sugʻorish ehtimol juda koʻp boʻlgan.
Endi siz: «Two neighbors, Farrux and Jasur, built identical wooden birdhouses from the same plan and hung them on the same day at the same height. Farrux hung his on a tree in a quiet corner of his garden; Jasur hung his on a tree of the same kind beside his busy front gate. By June, birds were nesting in the birdhouse in the garden, while the one by the gate stayed empty. The birds most likely chose the birdhouse ______»
Bir xil: chizma, kun, balandlik, daraxt turi.
Farq: bogʻning sokin burchagi yoki gavjum darvoza.
Natija: qushlar faqat bogʻdagi uyachada in qurgan.
Yagona farq nimani koʻrsatadi?
body.ru:
Пример: «Aziza grew mint in two identical pots on the same windowsill, with the same soil and water. She watered one pot every day and the other every third day. The pot watered every day wilted and turned yellow.»
Одинаково: горшки, подоконник, земля, вода.
Различие: как часто она поливала.
Результат: мяте в горшке с ежедневным поливом хуже. Значит, этой мяте ежедневный полив, вероятно, был слишком частым.
Теперь попробуйте сами: «Two neighbors, Farrux and Jasur, built identical wooden birdhouses from the same plan and hung them on the same day at the same height. Farrux hung his on a tree in a quiet corner of his garden; Jasur hung his on a tree of the same kind beside his busy front gate. By June, birds were nesting in the birdhouse in the garden, while the one by the gate stayed empty. The birds most likely chose the birdhouse ______»
Одинаково: чертёж, день, высота, порода дерева.
Различие: тихий угол сада или оживлённое место у ворот.
Результат: птицы гнездятся только в домике в саду.
Что показывает единственное различие?

body.en:
Watch out for three traps in comparison texts.
1. A shared thing explains nothing. If both groups had the same weather, the weather cannot explain why their results differ.
2. Too wide. The test shows something about these plants, this cake or this class. An ending about "every" plant or "all" students goes too far.
3. Same result, no effect. If both groups did equally well, the one difference did not matter here. It does not mean that both ways are bad, or that nothing ever matters.
Before you choose, ask: is this ending about the one thing that differed?
body.uz:
Taqqoslash matnlarida uchta tuzoqdan ehtiyot boʻling.
1. Umumiy narsa hech narsani tushuntirmaydi. Ikkala guruhda ob-havo bir xil boʻlsa, natijalar nega farq qilganini ob-havo tushuntira olmaydi.
2. Juda keng. Sinov shu oʻsimliklar, shu tort yoki shu sinf haqida nimanidir koʻrsatadi. «Every» oʻsimlik yoki «all» oʻquvchilar haqidagi davom haddan oshadi.
3. Natija bir xil — taʼsir yoʻq. Ikkala guruh bir xil natija koʻrsatsa, yagona farq bu yerda ahamiyatsiz boʻlgan. Bu ikkala usul ham yomon yoki hech narsa hech qachon muhim emas degani emas.
Tanlashdan oldin oʻzingizdan soʻrang: bu davom farq qilgan oʻsha yagona narsa haqidami?
body.ru:
Осторожно, в текстах-сравнениях три ловушки.
1. Общее ничего не объясняет. Если у обеих групп была одна погода, погода не объяснит, почему результаты разные.
2. Слишком широко. Проверка говорит об этих растениях, этом торте или этом классе. Окончание про «every» растение или «all» учеников заходит слишком далеко.
3. Одинаковый результат — нет влияния. Если обе группы справились одинаково, различие здесь не сыграло роли. Это не значит, что оба способа плохи или что ничто никогда не важно.
Прежде чем выбрать, спросите: это окончание про то единственное, что различалось?

title.en: SAT R&W: Inferences: chains, conditions and causes ruled out
title.uz: SAT R&W: Inferences — zanjir, shart va istisno qilingan sabab
title.ru: SAT R&W: Inferences — цепочки, условия и исключённые причины

body.en:
The hardest inference texts hide the answer behind one of three shapes.
1. A chain. A means B, and B means C. Write the links in a row, A → B → C. The blank is usually A → C.
2. A cause ruled out. The text names possible causes and shows that some cannot be right ("but the radio worked with new batteries"). Cross them out; the blank names what is left.
3. A condition:
• only if X, then Y: no X, no Y
• Y unless X: without X, Y happens
• not Y until X: Y never comes before X
Then take the smallest step the text supports. If it gives one case or one story, the ending says "may" or "suggests", not "proves", "always" or "all". In a story or a formal text the rules are the same: use only what the text says.
body.uz:
Eng qiyin Inferences matnlari javobni uch shakldan birining ortiga yashiradi.
1. Zanjir. A dan B kelib chiqadi, B dan C. Boʻgʻinlarni qatorga yozing: A → B → C. Boʻsh joy odatda A → C.
2. Istisno qilingan sabab. Matn ehtimoliy sabablarni aytadi va baʼzilari toʻgʻri boʻla olmasligini koʻrsatadi («but the radio worked with new batteries»). Ularni chizib tashlang; boʻsh joy qolganini aytadi.
3. Shart:
• only if X, then Y: X yoʻq — Y yoʻq
• Y unless X: X boʻlmasa, Y boʻladi
• not Y until X: Y hech qachon X dan oldin kelmaydi
Keyin matn asoslay oladigan eng kichik qadamni tanlang. Matn bitta holat yoki bitta hikoya bersa, davom «may» yoki «suggests» deydi, «proves», «always» yoki «all» emas. Hikoyada yoki rasmiy matnda ham qoida bir xil: faqat matnda aytilganidan foydalaning.
body.ru:
Самые трудные тексты Inferences прячут ответ за одной из трёх форм.
1. Цепочка. Из A следует B, из B следует C. Запишите звенья в ряд: A → B → C. Пропуск обычно — A → C.
2. Исключённая причина. Текст называет возможные причины и показывает, что некоторые не подходят («but the radio worked with new batteries»). Вычеркните их; пропуск называет то, что осталось.
3. Условие:
• only if X, then Y: нет X — нет Y
• Y unless X: без X будет Y
• not Y until X: Y никогда не наступает раньше X
Затем сделайте самый маленький шаг, который допускает текст. Если в нём один случай или одна история, окончание говорит «may» или «suggests», а не «proves», «always» или «all». В рассказе или официальном тексте правила те же: только то, что сказано в тексте.

body.en:
Worked example: "The milk in the jug had gone sour by noon. It had been bought that morning, so it was not old. The jug had just been washed, so it was not dirty. The kitchen was very hot that day."
Possible causes: old milk, a dirty jug, the heat.
Old milk: crossed out. A dirty jug: crossed out.
Left: the heat most likely turned the milk sour.
Now you: "Dilnoza could not get her desk lamp to turn on. Her brother blamed the bulb, but when she screwed it into the kitchen lamp, it lit at once. She then plugged her phone charger into the socket the desk lamp had been using, and the phone began to charge normally. Since neither the bulb nor the socket is at fault, the problem most likely ______"
Possible causes: the bulb, the socket, the power to the whole flat, the lamp itself.
The bulb lit in the kitchen lamp: crossed out.
The charger worked in the same socket: the socket and the power are crossed out.
What is left?
body.uz:
Namuna: «The milk in the jug had gone sour by noon. It had been bought that morning, so it was not old. The jug had just been washed, so it was not dirty. The kitchen was very hot that day.»
Ehtimoliy sabablar: eski sut, iflos koʻza, issiq.
Eski sut: chizib tashlandi. Iflos koʻza: chizib tashlandi.
Qolgani: sutni ehtimol issiq achitgan.
Endi siz: «Dilnoza could not get her desk lamp to turn on. Her brother blamed the bulb, but when she screwed it into the kitchen lamp, it lit at once. She then plugged her phone charger into the socket the desk lamp had been using, and the phone began to charge normally. Since neither the bulb nor the socket is at fault, the problem most likely ______»
Ehtimoliy sabablar: lampochka, rozetka, butun xonadondagi tok, chiroqning oʻzi.
Lampochka oshxona chirogʻida yondi: chizib tashlandi.
Quvvatlagich oʻsha rozetkada ishladi: rozetka ham, tok ham chizib tashlandi.
Nima qoldi?
body.ru:
Пример: «The milk in the jug had gone sour by noon. It had been bought that morning, so it was not old. The jug had just been washed, so it was not dirty. The kitchen was very hot that day.»
Возможные причины: старое молоко, грязный кувшин, жара.
Старое молоко: вычеркнуто. Грязный кувшин: вычеркнут.
Осталось: молоко, вероятно, скисло от жары.
Теперь попробуйте сами: «Dilnoza could not get her desk lamp to turn on. Her brother blamed the bulb, but when she screwed it into the kitchen lamp, it lit at once. She then plugged her phone charger into the socket the desk lamp had been using, and the phone began to charge normally. Since neither the bulb nor the socket is at fault, the problem most likely ______»
Возможные причины: лампочка, розетка, ток во всей квартире, сама лампа.
Лампочка загорелась в кухонной лампе: вычеркнута.
Зарядка работала в той же розетке: розетка и ток вычеркнуты.
Что осталось?

body.en:
Watch out for four traps.
1. A condition turned around. "The gate opens only if you have a card" means no card, no entry. It does not say that every card opens the gate.
2. A cause brought back. When the text has ruled out a cause, an ending that names it again is wrong, however natural it sounds.
3. A chain stretched. A → B → C supports A → C, not A → D. Stop where the last link stops.
4. Too big a step. One case gives "may" or "suggests". An ending with "proves", "always" or "never" claims more than one case can show.
body.uz:
Toʻrtta tuzoqdan ehtiyot boʻling.
1. Teskari aylantirilgan shart. «The gate opens only if you have a card» — karta boʻlmasa, kirish yoʻq degani. Bu har qanday karta darvozani ochadi degani emas.
2. Qaytarib olib kelingan sabab. Matn sababni istisno qilgan boʻlsa, uni yana aytgan davom qanchalik tabiiy tuyulmasin, xato.
3. Choʻzilgan zanjir. A → B → C faqat A → C ni asoslaydi, A → D ni emas. Oxirgi boʻgʻin qayerda tugasa, oʻsha yerda toʻxtang.
4. Juda katta qadam. Bitta holat «may» yoki «suggests» beradi. «Proves», «always» yoki «never» bilan kelgan davom bitta holat koʻrsata oladiganidan koʻp narsani daʼvo qiladi.
body.ru:
Осторожно, четыре ловушки.
1. Перевёрнутое условие. «The gate opens only if you have a card» значит: нет карты — нет входа. Это не значит, что любая карта открывает ворота.
2. Возвращённая причина. Если текст исключил причину, окончание, которое снова её называет, неверно, как бы естественно оно ни звучало.
3. Растянутая цепочка. A → B → C даёт A → C, но не A → D. Остановитесь там, где кончается последнее звено.
4. Слишком большой шаг. Один случай даёт «may» или «suggests». Окончание с «proves», «always» или «never» утверждает больше, чем может показать один случай.

stem.en:
Text 1
When the new outdoor gym opened in the park near the home of Sardor, the park keeper counted the visitors every evening. In the first two weeks, almost two hundred people a day used the machines. The keeper concluded that the gym had made the park a far more popular place.

Text 2
New equipment always draws a crowd at first: people come to try it and to watch their neighbors on it. A count from the first two weeks says little about the months ahead. Only a count taken after the novelty has worn off could show whether the park is truly busier.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the park keeper's conclusion in Text 1?

options.en: By arguing that a count from the first weeks is too short to support it
By suggesting that people came to the park for some reason other than the gym
By agreeing that the new gym will keep the park busy for years to come
By claiming that the park keeper counted the evening visitors incorrectly

why.en: Text 2 says a count from the first two weeks "says little about the months ahead": the crowd may be novelty, so the time is too short for the conclusion.
why.uz: Text 2 ikki haftalik hisob «says little about the months ahead» deydi: olomon yangilik tufayli boʻlishi mumkin, xulosa uchun vaqt juda qisqa.
why.ru: Text 2: подсчёт за первые две недели «says little about the months ahead»; людей может быть много просто из-за новизны, срок слишком короткий для вывода.

instructions.en: Read both texts. Decide how the ideas in them relate to each other.
instructions.uz: Ikkala matnni oʻqing. Ulardagi gʻoyalar bir-biri bilan qanday bogʻlanishini aniqlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
Text 1
Last autumn, the school library moved its soft chairs from a dark corner to the big windows. By December, students were borrowing a third more books than before. The librarian, Ms. Karimova, believes that the better light is what made students want to read.

Text 2
Borrowing at the library did rise last autumn. In the same months, however, the English teachers started a reading contest, and students earned points for every book they took home. A rise that large may owe more to the contest than to the chairs.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the librarian's explanation in Text 1?

options.en: By pointing out that another change at the same time may explain the rise
By doubting that students borrowed more books last autumn than before
By agreeing that the better light was the main reason the students read more
By arguing that the soft chairs should be moved back to the dark corner

why.en: Text 2 accepts that borrowing "did rise" but names the reading contest of the same months as a cause that may explain it better than the light.
why.uz: Text 2 kitob olish «did rise» ekanini qabul qiladi, lekin oʻsha oylardagi oʻqish tanlovini yorugʻlikdan koʻra yaxshiroq tushuntiradigan sabab deydi.
why.ru: Text 2 признаёт, что выдача «did rise», но называет конкурс чтения тех же месяцев: он может объяснить рост лучше света.

instructions.en: Read both texts. Decide how the ideas in them relate to each other.
instructions.uz: Ikkala matnni oʻqing. Ulardagi gʻoyalar bir-biri bilan qanday bogʻlanishini aniqlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
Text 1
The neighborhood committee plans to turn the empty lot behind the row of shops into a parking area. Drivers now circle the block for twenty minutes looking for a space, and the shop owners say they lose customers who simply give up and drive away.

Text 2
A parking area would bring more cars, and the shops would surely gain customers. But the empty lot is also where the children of the block play football, since the nearest playground lies across a busy road. Paving the lot would send them into that road.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the committee's plan in Text 1?

options.en: By granting that it would help the shops but warning that it would put children in danger
By arguing that a parking area behind the shops would not bring them any more customers at all
By agreeing that the empty lot is of no real use to anyone who lives in the neighborhood now
By suggesting that the shop owners should pay for a new playground on the far side of the road

why.en: Text 2 grants that "the shops would surely gain customers" but adds a cost: paving the lot would send the children who play there into a busy road.
why.uz: Text 2 «the shops would surely gain customers» ekanini tan oladi, lekin xarajat qoʻshadi: maydon asfaltlansa, u yerda oʻynaydigan bolalar gavjum yoʻlga chiqadi.
why.ru: Text 2 признаёт, что «the shops would surely gain customers», но добавляет цену: без пустыря играющие там дети уйдут на оживлённую дорогу.

instructions.en: Read both texts. Decide how the ideas in them relate to each other.
instructions.uz: Ikkala matnni oʻqing. Ulardagi gʻoyalar bir-biri bilan qanday bogʻlanishini aniqlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
Text 1
On our school basketball team, I pick players only from those who come to every practice. Skill can be taught, but a player who skips practice lets the whole team down, however talented she is.

Text 2
This year a talented new student joined our school in the middle of the season. She had missed the first month of practice, so she could not be picked. The team might have done better with a rule that judged players by how well they play.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the suggestion in Text 2?

options.en: By arguing that coming to practice matters more than talent alone
By agreeing that the new student should have been picked for the team at once
By claiming that the new student was not a very talented player
By suggesting that the team should hold its practices less often

why.en: Text 1 picks only players who never miss practice, "however talented she is": its author would put practice above skill and reject a rule based on skill alone.
why.uz: Text 1 muallifi faqat mashgʻulotni qoldirmaydiganlarni tanlaydi, «however talented she is»: u mahoratdan koʻra qatnashishni ustun qoʻyadi va faqat mahoratga asoslangan qoidani rad etadi.
why.ru: Автор Text 1 берёт только тех, кто не пропускает тренировки, «however talented she is»: посещение для него важнее таланта.

instructions.en: Read both texts. Decide how the ideas in them relate to each other.
instructions.uz: Ikkala matnni oʻqing. Ulardagi gʻoyalar bir-biri bilan qanday bogʻlanishini aniqlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
Text 1
Shoppers in our district now carry home far fewer plastic bags than they did five years ago. The reason, in my view, is the small fee that shops began charging for each bag: people dislike paying for something that used to be free, however little it costs.

Text 2
There is no doubt that fewer plastic bags leave the shops in our district today. The fee, though, is too small to change how people shop. What changed them was the school campaign in which children sewed and decorated cloth bags and took them home; parents simply use the bags their children made.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

options.en: Shoppers in the district use fewer plastic bags than they did in the past.
The fee for each bag is the main reason shoppers changed their habits.
Children should sew new cloth bags at school every year.
The fee for plastic bags in the district should be raised.

why.en: Text 1 says "far fewer plastic bags" go home; Text 2 says there is "no doubt" fewer leave the shops. They split only on the reason: the fee or the cloth bags.
why.uz: Text 1 «far fewer plastic bags» deydi; Text 2 ham kamroq paket chiqishiga «no doubt» deydi. Ular faqat sababda ajralishadi: toʻlov yoki mato sumka.
why.ru: Text 1: «far fewer plastic bags»; Text 2: в том, что пакетов меньше, «no doubt». Расходятся они лишь в причине: плата или тканевые сумки.

instructions.en: Read both texts. Decide how the ideas in them relate to each other.
instructions.uz: Ikkala matnni oʻqing. Ulardagi gʻoyalar bir-biri bilan qanday bogʻlanishini aniqlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
Text 1
Old houses in the center of a town are often torn down because repairing them costs more than building anew. Yet once such a house is gone, it cannot be brought back, and a street of new buildings loses the character that drew people to it. A town should pay part of the repair costs for owners who keep their old houses.

Text 2
It is true that old houses give a street its character, and that repairs are costly. But public money is limited, and a town that pays for private repairs has less to spend on schools and clinics. Owners who choose to keep an old house should carry the cost themselves.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the proposal in Text 2?

options.en: By warning that leaving the whole cost to owners would lead to more old houses being lost
By agreeing that public money should go to schools and clinics before old houses
By denying that repairing an old house costs more than building a new one
By claiming that new buildings give a street more character than old houses do

why.en: Text 1 says high repair costs are why old houses are torn down and asks the town to share them; leaving owners the whole cost would mean more houses lost.
why.uz: Text 1 eski uylar taʼmir qimmatligi sabab buziladi deydi va xarajatni shahar ham boʻlishib koʻtarsin deydi; hammasi egaga qolsa, koʻproq uy yoʻqoladi.
why.ru: Text 1: старые дома сносят из-за дорогого ремонта, и город должен помочь; если всё платит владелец, домов будет теряться больше.

instructions.en: Read both texts. Decide how the ideas in them relate to each other.
instructions.uz: Ikkala matnni oʻqing. Ulardagi gʻoyalar bir-biri bilan qanday bogʻlanishini aniqlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте оба текста. Определите, как связаны их идеи.

stem.en:
To see whether the brand of flour matters, Ozoda baked two cakes on the same afternoon with the same eggs, sugar and oven, one with an expensive flour and one with the cheapest flour in the shop. Her family tasted both without knowing which was which, and no one could tell them apart. Ozoda most likely concluded that, for this cake, ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the cheaper flour worked as well as the expensive one.
the expensive flour gave a much lighter and softer cake.
the oven had been far too hot for both of the cakes.
the brand of flour makes no difference in any baking.

why.en: Everything but the flour was the same, and no one could tell the cakes apart, so for this cake the cheap flour did as well as the expensive one.
why.uz: Un turidan tashqari hamma narsa bir xil edi va hech kim tortlarni ajrata olmadi: bu tort uchun arzon un qimmatidek yaxshi chiqqan.
why.ru: Всё, кроме муки, было одинаково, и никто не отличил торты, значит, для этого торта дешёвая мука сработала не хуже дорогой.

instructions.en: Read the text. Choose the ending that follows most logically from it.
instructions.uz: Matnni oʻqing. Undan mantiqan eng toʻgʻri kelib chiqadigan davomni tanlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте текст. Выберите окончание, которое логичнее всего из него следует.

stem.en:
Two neighbors, Farrux and Jasur, built identical wooden birdhouses from the same plan and hung them on the same day at the same height. Farrux hung his on a tree in a quiet corner of his garden; Jasur hung his on a tree of the same kind beside his busy front gate. By June, birds were nesting in the birdhouse in the garden, while the one by the gate stayed empty. The birds most likely chose the birdhouse ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: that was farther from people passing by.
that had been built from a better plan.
that was hung earlier in the spring.
that was on the taller of the two trees.

why.en: The birdhouses differed only in place: a quiet garden corner or a busy gate. Birds chose the quiet one, so distance from passers-by most likely mattered.
why.uz: Uyachalar faqat joyi bilan farq qilgan: bogʻning sokin burchagi yoki gavjum darvoza. Qushlar sokinini tanladi, demak oʻtkinchilardan uzoqlik ehtimol muhim boʻlgan.
why.ru: Домики различались только местом: тихий угол сада или оживлённое место у ворот. Птицы выбрали тихий, значит, вероятно, важна была удалённость от прохожих.

instructions.en: Read the text. Choose the ending that follows most logically from it.
instructions.uz: Matnni oʻqing. Undan mantiqan eng toʻgʻri kelib chiqadigan davomni tanlang.
instructions.ru: Прочитайте текст. Выберите окончание, которое логичнее всего из него следует.

stem.en:
A sports teacher timed two groups of students over the same 400-meter run, on the same track and on the same cool morning. Both groups had trained three times a week for two months, but one group had warmed up by jogging slowly for ten minutes before each session, while the other had skipped the warm-up. In the final run, the group that warmed up was faster on average. Because both groups trained equally often, the difference in their times ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: cannot be explained by how often they trained.
proves that warming up makes every runner faster.
was most likely caused by the cool weather that morning.
shows that training three times a week is too little.

why.en: Both groups trained equally often, so how often they trained cannot explain why their times differ; the cool morning was shared too.
why.uz: Ikkala guruh bir xil tez-tez mashq qilgan, shuning uchun mashq soni vaqtlardagi farqni tushuntira olmaydi; salqin tong ham umumiy edi.
why.ru: Обе группы тренировались одинаково часто, поэтому частота тренировок не объясняет разницу во времени; прохладное утро тоже было общим.

stem.en:
Sherzod is learning to drive with his uncle, who never breaks his own rules. The uncle has one firm rule: Sherzod may not drive on the main road until he has driven the quiet village roads for twenty hours without a single mistake. Last week Sherzod drove on the main road for the first time. It can be inferred that by last week Sherzod ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: had driven twenty hours on the quiet roads without a mistake.
had never driven on the quiet roads of the village.
had made several mistakes on the quiet village roads.
would soon be allowed to drive on any road in any city he liked.

why.en: The rule says "not until" twenty mistake-free hours on quiet roads, and the uncle never breaks it, so Sherzod had already done those hours.
why.uz: Qoida «not until» deydi: avval sokin yoʻllarda xatosiz yigirma soat; amaki qoidani buzmaydi, demak Sherzod bu soatlarni oʻtagan.
why.ru: Правило «not until»: сначала двадцать часов без ошибок на тихих дорогах; дядя правил не нарушает, значит, Шерзод эти часы уже проехал.

stem.en:
Dilnoza could not get her desk lamp to turn on. Her brother blamed the bulb, but when she screwed it into the kitchen lamp, it lit at once. She then plugged her phone charger into the socket the desk lamp had been using, and the phone began to charge normally. Since neither the bulb nor the socket is at fault, the problem most likely ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: lies somewhere in the desk lamp itself, such as its cable or switch.
lies in the bulb, which seems to work only when it is in the kitchen lamp.
lies in the socket, which cannot power a lamp and a charger.
lies in the power supply to the whole flat.

why.en: The bulb lit in another lamp and the socket charged a phone, so both are ruled out, and the flat has power; what is left is the lamp itself.
why.uz: Lampochka boshqa chiroqda yondi, rozetka telefonni quvvatladi: ikkalasi istisno, xonadonda tok bor; qolgani chiroqning oʻzi.
why.ru: Лампочка горит в другой лампе, розетка заряжает телефон: обе исключены, ток в квартире есть; остаётся сама настольная лампа.

stem.en:
The school canteen buys its bread only from bakers who use flour from local mills. The only baker in the town who uses such flour is Mr. Qodirov, and this month he has closed his shop for repairs. This month, therefore, the canteen most likely ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: cannot buy its bread from any baker in the town.
buys its bread from another of the bakers in the town.
buys bread made with flour from distant mills.
has closed its kitchen until the shop reopens.

why.en: The canteen buys only local-flour bread, only Mr. Qodirov in town bakes it, and he is closed: so no baker in the town can supply it this month.
why.uz: Zanjir: oshxona faqat mahalliy unli non oladi, shaharda uni faqat Qodirov yopadi, u yopiq. Demak bu oy shahardagi hech bir novvoy non bera olmaydi.
why.ru: Цепочка: столовая берёт хлеб только на местной муке, в городе его печёт лишь пекарь Кодиров, а его пекарня закрыта. Значит, никто из пекарей города в этом месяце такой хлеб не поставит.
